claim.why_it_matters: Two headwords merged on one line, and the right column (through Files / Relative 178) loses its sub-entry indentation. The index is informative, but a flattened or merged index entry misattributes page references to the wrong headword.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered page 936 (printed index page 912), right column under 'F': 'FACTORIAL function 668' and 'FACTORY clause' are two separate headword lines, with 'METHOD-ID paragraph 215' indented as a sub-entry of FACTORY clause. page-936.md line 61 reads 'FACTORIAL function 668 FACTORY clause' as one line. From line 63 to 'Relative 178', every right-column line has the same 3-space indent, so headwords such as 'Factory data 199, 839', 'FALSE phrase', 'File' and 'Files 176, 773' cannot be told apart from their sub-entries ('EVALUATE statement 493', 'logical 176', 'Indexed 178'). The PDF shows two indent levels. The merge makes '668' look like it belongs to a combined 'FACTORIAL function ... FACTORY clause' entry, and the flattening hides which headword owns each sub-entry's page reference. This is a real structural defect in the informative index, and the claim describes it accurately. A separate artifact on the same page, outside this claim: the markdown repeats 'FILE-CONTROL paragraph 248' twice, while the PDF has the sub-entry 'FILE-CONTROL paragraph 248' under FILE STATUS clause and then the headword 'FILE-CONTROL paragraph 248'.
